description: Ask the game that godot_session started. op `tree` (the live node tree: path, class, script; root, depth, limit), `get` (values now: watch ["Hero.position", "Hero.is_on_floor()"]), `set` (target "Hero.position", value "Vector3(0, 30, 0)" as Godot writes values), `call` (node, method, args), `eval` (a Godot Expression with the scene root as base, e.g. get_node("Hero").velocity.length()), `step` (play `frames` frames with an `input` timeline counted from this step, sample `watch`, stop early `until` a condition holds; the same frame-exact input as godot_play), `signals` (record these signals; later steps list when they fired), `layout` (3D objects: global position, size, lowest point, and whether each rests on, floats above or sinks into what is below, plus scale mistakes), `ray` (from, to: what a physics ray hits), `ui` (visible controls at one or more window `sizes`, with clipped text, off-screen panels, overlapping buttons and small targets), `errors` (what the game printed since the last call), `reload` (load the scripts you edited into the running game: every node keeps its values and runs the new code from the next step, so you try a fix without loading the world again; `files`, default every script changed since the last reload; a script that does not compile is left as it was). Every answer ends with the errors and warnings the game printed since the last call, runtime errors with their call chain. Time only moves on a step, so the session stays deterministic. Use it to try a fix live, find a state that is hard to reach, or watch a long scenario in parts.

every.description: step: sample every n frames (default: about 10 samples)

files.description: reload: res:// scripts to reload (default: every script changed since the session started or the last reload)

input.description: step: "0 press jump; 10 release jump; 20 hold right 30"

node.description: call: node path from the scene root

path.description: The project folder, or any file or folder inside it (Godotwright walks up to project.godot). Relative paths start at the server's folder. Default: the current project.

root.description: tree: start at this node (default the scene root)

sizes.description: ui: window sizes such as 1280x720 or 720x1280 (default the size the project sets)

until.description: step: stop at the first frame where this holds, "Hero.is_on_floor() == true"

value.description: set: the new value as Godot writes it

watch.description: get and step: values to read, Node.property or Node.method()

name: godot_game
title: Look at and drive the running game session
